newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold subdued on limited India buying.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold subdued on limited India buying.

text.p: Dubai's gold market remained subdued as Indian bullion demand maintained its seasonal downturn, gold traders and wholesalers said on Sunday.

Re-exports of gold and silver to India -- the world's largest consumer of the yellow metal -- were capped by a lack of Indian wedding demand which is not expected to resurface until the end of India's June to September monsoon season.
Weaker prices had failed to ignite buying which was not expected to resume until late July when Indian agricultural communities would have crop income to spend, traders said.
"Most of my Indian clients have gone on holiday so business has slowed down. I do not expect it to pick up for at least another month," said one Indian trader based in Dubai.

Dubai gold prices headed down in line with world markets though not below the $340 an ounce mark which was seen necessary to galvanise Indian-subcontinent demand which pushed Dubai's own bullion imports to record highs earlier this year.
The Gulf Arab emirate is India's main source of gold. Import figures into Dubai for May are due for release late next week.
"It would take a fall to $325 to get people's interest back in this market...People bought gold in the shopping festival so why should they buy again now," said one trader.
The month-long and state-sponsored Dubai shopping festival in April had prompted a major buying spree on jewellery, reducing current consumer spending power.
Dubai's benchmark ten tola bar -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- was quoted at 4,755 UAE dirhams ($1,295) on Sunday from 4,765 dirhams ($1,298) a week earlier.
International spot bullion was last quoted on Saturday at $343.70/344.20 an ounce from $344.70/345.20 last week.
Turnover in the Dubai souk was also on the downturn because of the end of the Gulf emirate's tourism season which brings in custom from European, North American and Russian visitors.
"Tourists are rarely coming to my shop now...Most people are leaving to go on their own holidays," said one trader. ($1=3.67 dirhams)
